# Setup

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(conflicted)
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)
library(mice)
library(ggmice)
library(ggrepel)
library(DT)
library(lmodel2)

set.seed(19347)

conflicts_prefer(dplyr::filter)
conflicts_prefer(dplyr::select)

options(DT.options = list(pageLength = 10))

theme_set(theme_minimal())

load("intermediate/SES.RData")

#process FD dataframe
results_sites <- results_sites |> 
  rename(year = date, site = plot)

years <- unique(results_all$date)
```

## Matrix product backend

Despite setting a seed, imputations with `mice()` from different machines or operating systems might differ slightly, while imputations from the same machine and OS should be fully reproducible. I narrowed this down to different matrix product implementations. To circumvent this problem, the following line sets NETLIB as default matrix backend (default on Windows) if available. Alternatively, use the provided `weather.RData` file in notebooks following this one.

```{r}
if (.Platform$OS.type == "unix"){
  library(flexiblas)
  if(flexiblas_avail() && "NETLIB" %in% flexiblas_list()){
    flexiblas_switch(flexiblas_load_backend("NETLIB"))
  }
  flexiblas_current_backend()
}
```

Based on the vegetation surveys, my years of interest are `{r} years`.

# Sample dates

The weather data will be summarized as annual means, starting as monthly averages. To respect causality, since the vegetation sampling was carried out in summer, instead of calculating the means for the solar year, we calculate it from the 12 months before the sampling in each case.
This chunk gets the date for each sampling, and makes a sequence of the 12 months before.

```{r}
#toy example
toy <- tibble(plot = 1:2,
              date = c("15/05/2001", "02/07/1999")) |> 
  mutate(date = dmy(date)) |> 
  mutate(year_before = date - years(1)) |> 
  mutate(month = map(year_before, \(x) x %m+% months(0:11))) |> 
  unnest(month) |> 
  mutate(year = year(month),
         month = month(month))
  
head(toy, 13)

#tibble to refer plot codes to plot names
site_lookup <- tibble(code_plot = c(1, 3, 4, 20),
                      site = c("01-ABR1", "03-CAL1", "04-CAM1", "20-VEN1"))

dates <- read_csv("Data/sample_dates.csv") |> 
  filter(code_country == 5) |> # Italy is 5
  filter(code_plot %in% site_lookup$code_plot) |> # only sites of interest
  filter(survey_year %in% years) |> # only years of interest
  filter(code_fence == 1) |> # only surveys inside the plot
  mutate(date_sampling = ymd(date_sampling)) |> 
  filter(month(date_sampling) |> between(6, 8)) |>  # take summer survey
  mutate(year_before = date_sampling - years(1)) |> 
  mutate(month = map(year_before, \(x) x %m+% months(0:11))) |> 
  unnest(month) |> 
  mutate(year = year(month),
         month = month(month)) |> 
  left_join(site_lookup)

head(dates, 13)

#check if exactly 1 each year, site, month
dates |>
  group_by(survey_year, site, month) |> 
  count() |> 
  ungroup() |> 
  tidyr::complete(survey_year, site, month = 1:12) |> 
  filter(n != 1)

#check if 12 for each survey and site
dates |> 
  group_by(site, survey_year) |> 
  count() |> 
  filter(n != 12)

#these are all the months required for weather data. Some will be missing
dates <- dates |> 
  select(site, survey_year, year, month)

#check whether all FD data appears in dates tibble
results_all |> 
  distinct(plot, date) |> 
  anti_join(dates |> 
              rename(plot = site, date = survey_year))

#check whether there are dates not corresponding to FD
dates |> 
  distinct(site, survey_year) |> 
  anti_join(results_all |> 
              rename(site = plot, survey_year = date))
```

There are some clear inconsistencies in the data. These should be removed before proceeding.

```{r}
# remove 20-VEN1 soil T ITP in 2010 and 2011
weat <- weat |> 
  mutate(soil_t_mean = replace_when(soil_t_mean, site == "20-VEN1" & year %in% 2010:2011 & type == "ITP" ~ NA))

# remove 03-CAL1 soil T OFD in 2013, 2014, 2015
weat <- weat |> 
  mutate(soil_t_mean = replace_when(soil_t_mean, site == "03-CAL1" & year %in% 2013:2015 & type == "OFD" ~ NA))

# remove 03-CAL1 solar radiation in July 2011
weat <- weat |> 
  mutate(across(c(solar_radiation_mean, solar_radiation_max), 
                \(x) replace_when(x, site == "03-CAL1" & year == 2011 & month == 7 ~ NA)))

# remove whole years with 0 precipitation
weat <- weat |> 
  mutate(precipitation = replace_when(precipitation, site == "01-ABR1" & year %in% c(2007, 2011, 2012) & type == "ITP" ~ NA,
                                      site == "03-CAL1" & year == 2015 & type == "OFD" ~ NA,
                                      site == "03-CAL1" & year == 2014 & type == "OFD" & month %in% 9:12 ~ NA))

```

## Calculating the number of months with weather data for each survey

We have a table which specifies, for each site and sampling year, the required months of weather data. Let's count how many of those are available.

```{r}
#only weather data relevant for vegetation surveys here
weat_mo <- weat |> 
  semi_join(dates)

datatable(weat_mo)

OFD <- weat_mo |> 
  filter(type == "OFD") |> 
  right_join(dates)

ITP <- weat_mo |> 
  filter(type == "ITP") |> 
  right_join(dates)
```

```{r}
months_OFD <- OFD |>

datatable(months_OFD)
```

```{r}
datatable(months_ITP)
```

# Keep complete OFD data

This is the first step in handling missing weather data. It is clear that monthly coverage is incomplete in some sites and years. This is due to malfunctioning of the stations and we assume there is no bias in omitting these data. This is possible for open-field data where there is good coverage in most site-years. The annual means are calculated from monthly averages, giving equal weight to each month.

```{r}
vars <- names(months_OFD) |> 
  str_subset("site|survey_year|_min|_max", negate = T)

#site-years with 11 or 12 months
OFD_keep <- map(vars, \(x) {
  months_OFD |>
    select(site, survey_year, all_of(x)) |>
    filter(.data[[x]] == 12)
  }) |> 
  set_names(vars)

#subset data
complete_OFD <- OFD_keep |> 
  imap(\(x, idx) OFD |>
        select(site, survey_year, all_of(idx)) |> 
        semi_join(x[,1:2]))

#annual means
complete_OFD <- complete_OFD |> 
  imap(\(x, idx) if(str_detect(idx, "precipitation")){
    #sum precipitation
    x |> 
      summarise("{idx}" := sum(.data[[idx]], na.rm = T),
                   .by = c(site, survey_year))
  } else {
    #average others
    x |> 
         summarise("{idx}" := mean(.data[[idx]], na.rm = T),
                   .by = c(site, survey_year))
  })
```

# Impute missing ITP data

Since missingness is higher for sub-canopy data, we choose imputation instead of complete-case analysis. This also allows presenting both approaches. 

```{r}
# convert weather data into wider format, so that OFD can be used to impute ITP
weat_imp <- weat |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = type,
    names_sep = "_",
    values_from = air_t_mean:wind_speed_max)
```

We are using canopy cover measured during surveys as one predictor of sub-canopy weather.

```{r}
# join canopy cover

cover <- read_csv("Data/cover.csv")

weat_imp <- weat_imp |> 
  left_join(cover)

# keep for later

weat_imp_raw <- weat_imp
```

The probability of missingness is affected by the site identity, so including this variable makes the missingness ignorable. For the imputation model and the analysis model to be *congenial*, the outcome variable should be included in the imputation [@dagostinomcgowan2024]. This leads to a compromise, because the outcome (FD) has replicate measurements for each year and site (subplots), while the weather data is site-level, but has monthly measurements. We need to perform imputation at the month level, even if the final model will be done on annual means, because missingness is not homogeneous and it can lead to considerable bias if done on pre-averaged data. The chosen solution is to treat the outcome as time-invariant within each year (a pratical assumption shared by the analysis model), and to use the mean of the subplots as a site-level summary. Both of these choices are widely accepted [@sterne2009; @white2011; @audigier2018].

```{r}
# average the "regional pool" SES-FD at a site level
FD_avg <- results_sites |> 
  group_by(year, site) |>
  select(!subplot) |> 
  summarise(across(everything(), mean), .groups = "drop")

# refer weather to survey
weat_imp <- weat_imp |> 
  full_join(dates, relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  #join FD
  left_join(FD_avg, by = join_by(survey_year == year, site)) |> 
  relocate(survey_year:below, .after = month)
```

The resulting tibble contains weather from years without a vegetation survey, which can be useful for imputation, but also years of vegetation surveys without any weather data. These can be removed.

```{r}
exclude <- weat_imp |> 
  filter(!is.na(survey_year)) |> # survey years
  group_by(site, survey_year) |> 
  # those that have 12 months of NA in all variables
  summarise(across(air_t_mean_OFD:wind_speed_max_ITP, \(x) sum(is.na(x))), .groups = "drop") |> 
  filter(if_all(air_t_mean_OFD:wind_speed_max_ITP, \(x) x == 12))

weat_imp <- weat_imp |> 
  anti_join(exclude |> select(site, survey_year)) |> 
  mutate(across(c(site, survey_year, year, month), as_factor))
```

## Proportion of missing data before imputation

For the three variables of interest, the percent of missing monthly data, considering only the months associated with a survey and excluding 04-CAM1, a site with no ITP data, is:

```{r}
weat_imp |> 
  semi_join(dates |> 
                select(site, survey_year) |> 
                mutate(across(everything(), as_factor))) |> 
  filter_out(site == "04-CAM1") |> 
  summarise(across(c(air_t_mean_ITP, soil_t_mean_ITP, precipitation_ITP), \(x) sum(is.na(x) / length(x) * 100)))
```

## Variables for imputation

The following patterns show that when means are missing, so are minima and maxima, so they are not useful for imputation:

```{r}
#air T
weat_imp |> 
  select(air_t_mean_OFD:air_t_max_ITP) |> 
  plot_pattern(rotate = T)

#soil T
weat_imp |> 
  select(soil_t_mean_OFD:soil_t_max_ITP) |> 
  plot_pattern(rotate = T)

#solar radiation
weat_imp |> 
  select(solar_radiation_mean_OFD:solar_radiation_max_ITP) |> 
  plot_pattern(rotate = T) # completely missing for ITP

#relative humidity
weat_imp |> 
  select(relative_humidity_mean_OFD:relative_humidity_max_ITP) |> 
  plot_pattern(rotate = T)

#wind speed
weat_imp |> 
  select(wind_speed_mean_OFD:wind_speed_max_ITP) |> 
  plot_pattern(rotate = T) # completely missing for ITP

#remove min and max columns
weat_imp <- weat_imp |> 
  select(!contains(c("min", "max"))) |> 
#remove empty columns
  select(!c(solar_radiation_mean_ITP, wind_speed_mean_ITP))
```

Influx and outflux patterns. Variables with high influx are easier to impute, variable with high outflux are more useful to impute other variables. As expected, OFD variables have higher outflux because missingness is generally lower.

```{r}
flux(weat_imp[-1:-7]) |> 
  select(c(influx, outflux)) |> 
  rownames_to_column() |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = influx, y = outflux))+
  geom_point()+
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = rowname))+
  annotate("segment", x = 0, y = 1, xend = 1, yend = 0)+
  lims(x = c(-0.5,1), y = 0:1)
```

The following correlation plot reveals an interesting pattern: there are two blocks of related variables, temperature/radiation and humidity/precipitation. Wind speed doesn't seem to be related to anything, and it's not used in the analysis models. This informs the selection of which variables to use in the imputation models.

```{r}
plot_corr(weat_imp[-1:-7], rotate = T, diagonal = T)

weat_imp <- weat_imp |> 
  select(!wind_speed_mean_OFD)

# identify variable blocks
temp_vars <- colnames(weat_imp)[8:12]

hum_vars <- colnames(weat_imp)[13:16]
```

The ideal case is having OFD data for missing ITP variables of the same block. This happens most of the times. It is also possible to exclude observations with all variables in a block missing.

```{r}
#| fig-asp: 3.5

#temperature
weat_imp |> 
  nest(.by = site) |> 
  deframe() |> 
  imap(\(data, site_name) data |> 
        select(any_of(c("year", "cover", "month", temp_vars))) |> 
        plot_pattern(rotate = T) +
        ggtitle(site_name)) |> 
  patchwork::wrap_plots(ncol = 1)

#precipitation
weat_imp |> 
  nest(.by = site) |> 
  deframe() |> 
  imap(\(data, site_name) data |> 
        select(any_of(c("year", "cover", "month", hum_vars))) |> 
        plot_pattern(rotate = T) +
        ggtitle(site_name)) |> 
  patchwork::wrap_plots(ncol = 1)
```

## Imputation proper

Next, we set up the imputation. We are using site as predictor: even if some levels are excluded for some outcomes, for lack of sufficient data in that site (especially 04-CAM1), it is better than ignoring it completely.

```{r}
# select outcome depending on analysis model (overall, aboveground, below) and generate separate imputations

imp_above <- weat_imp |> 
  select(site:survey_year, above, air_t_mean_OFD:cover)

imp_below <- weat_imp |> 
  select(site:survey_year, below, air_t_mean_OFD:cover)

imp_overall <- weat_imp |> 
  select(site:survey_year, overall, air_t_mean_OFD:cover)

# don't impute survey_year, this variable is just for later

method_ab <- make.method(imp_above)
method_ab["survey_year"] <- ""

method_bl <- make.method(imp_below)
method_bl["survey_year"] <- ""

method_oa <- make.method(imp_overall)
method_oa["survey_year"] <- ""

#make predictor matrix
predmat_ab <- imp_above |> 
  quickpred(include = c("above", "month"), exclude = "survey_year")

#exclude outcomes which are not imputed for clarity
predmat_ab[which(method_ab == ""),] <- 0

#plot
plot_pred(predmat_ab, rotate = T)

#copy for other FDs
predmat_bl <- predmat_oa <- predmat_ab

colnames(predmat_bl)[5] <- "below"
rownames(predmat_bl)[5] <- "below"

colnames(predmat_oa)[5] <- "overall"
rownames(predmat_oa)[5] <- "overall"
```

```{r}
imp_above <- imp_above |> 
  mice(predictorMatrix = predmat_ab,
       method = method_ab,
       m = 5, maxit = 100,
       seed = 8274, printFlag = F)

imp_below <- imp_below |> 
   mice(predictorMatrix = predmat_bl,
        method = method_bl,
        m = 5, maxit = 100,
        seed = 8274, printFlag = F)

imp_overall <- imp_overall |> 
   mice(predictorMatrix = predmat_oa,
        method = method_oa,
        m = 5, maxit = 100,
        seed = 8274, printFlag = F)

#complete and keep only data corresponding to FD surveys
complete_above <- complete(imp_above, action = "long") |> 
  semi_join(dates |> mutate(across(everything(), as_factor)))

complete_below <- complete(imp_below, action = "long") |> 
  semi_join(dates |> mutate(across(everything(), as_factor)))

complete_overall <- complete(imp_overall, action = "long") |> 
  semi_join(dates |> mutate(across(everything(), as_factor)))

```

## Imputation diagnostics

Check for NAs, convergence, differences between imputations, imputed against observed data. Since there is heterogeneity in months, the latter is done by month.

```{r}
#plotting functions
#box plot
bwplot_imp <- function(data, vars) {
  map(vars, 
      ~ {
        ggmice(data, aes(x = .imp, y = .data[[.x]])) +
          geom_boxplot() +
          labs(x = "Imputation number")
      }
  ) |> 
    patchwork::wrap_plots()&
    theme(legend.position = "none")
}

#density plot
densplot_imp <- function(data, vars) {
  map(vars, 
      ~ {
        ggmice(data, aes(x = .data[[.x]], group = .imp, size = .where)) +
          geom_density()+
          scale_size_manual(
            values = c("observed" = 1, "imputed" = 0.5),
            guide = "none")+
          facet_wrap(~month,
                     ncol = 3,
                     strip.position = "right",
                     scales = "free_y",
                     dir = "v")+
          theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 8))+
          ggtitle("month")
      }) |> 
    patchwork::wrap_plots(guides = "collect", ncol = 1)&
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}

#convergence plot
convplot_imp <- function(data, dia = psrf){
  convergence(data) |> 
    filter_out(is.na({{dia}})) |> 
    ggplot(aes(x = .it, y = {{dia}})) +
    geom_line() +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = 2, alpha = 0.5) +
    facet_wrap(~vrb)
}

# outcome variables 
to_plot <- c("air_t_mean_ITP", "soil_t_mean_ITP", "precipitation_ITP", "relative_humidity_mean_ITP")
```

## Open-field data

## Sub-canopy data

Here are the annual means for each of the multiple imputations. It is clear that there is much more uncertainty for 04-CAM1, the site with more missing data. Using the multiply imputed datasets will reflect this uncertainty in the analysis.

```{r}
plot_complete <- function(x){
  x |> 
    select(c(site, survey_year, .imp, .id, contains("ITP"))) |> 
    mutate(survey_year = as.numeric(levels(survey_year)[survey_year])) |> 
    group_by(site, survey_year, .imp) |> 
    summarise(across(everything(), mean), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(precipitation_ITP = precipitation_ITP * 12) |> 
    pivot_longer(contains("ITP"), names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") |> 
    ggplot(aes(x = survey_year, y = value, color = site))+
    geom_point()+
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = F, linewidth = 0.5)+
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(2000, 2011),
                     breaks = scales::breaks_width(1))+
    facet_wrap(~variable, scales = "free_y")+
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90))
}

complete_above |> 
  plot_complete() +
  ggtitle("Multiple imputations for aboveground FD analysis")

complete_below |> 
  plot_complete() +
  ggtitle("Multiple imputations for belowground FD analysis")
  
complete_overall |> 
  plot_complete() +
  ggtitle("Multiple imputations for overall FD analysis")
```


# Correlations, MA regressions, and SD ratios

To evaluate the extent to which air temperature and precipitation measured by sub-canopy stations are different from open-field measurements (for example, lower because of buffering and stemflow), I use correlations, major axis regressions and SD ratios, pooling the results across the imputations.

```{r}
cor_pool <- function(dat, var1, var2){
  imp_overall |> 
    miceadds::micombine.cor(c(var1, var2)) |> 
    slice(1) |> 
    select(est = r, lo = lower95, hi = upper95)
  }

sdratio_pool <- function(dat, var1, var2){
  pooled <- dat |>
    complete(action = "long") |> 
    summarise(q_lsd = log(sd(.data[[var1]]) / sd(.data[[var2]])),
              u_lsd = (1 - cor(.data[[var1]], .data[[var2]])^2) / (n() - 1),
              .by = .imp) |>
    with(pool.scalar(q_lsd, u_lsd))

  est <- pooled$qbar
  int <- 2*sqrt(pooled$t)

  tibble(est = est, lo = est - int, hi = est + int) |> 
    exp()
}

MA_pool <- function(dat, var1, var2){
  form <- as.formula(str_c(var1, "~", var2))
  pooled <- dat |> 
    complete(action = "all") |> 
    map(\(x) suppressMessages(lmodel2(form, x)) |> 
          broom::tidy() |> 
          filter(method == "MA" & term == "Slope") |> 
          mutate(var = (mean(c(conf.high - estimate,
                             estimate - conf.low))/2)^2)) |> 
  bind_rows() |> 
    with(pool.scalar(estimate, var))
  
  est <- pooled$qbar
  int <- 2*sqrt(pooled$t)

  tibble(est = est, lo = est - int, hi = est + int)
}
```

The following table reports correlations, SD ratios and MA slopes with approximate 95% CIs:

```{r}
itp_ofd <- tibble(var = c("air_t_mean", "precipitation"),
       vars = map(var, \(x) c(str_c(x, "_ITP"), str_c(x, "_OFD")))) |> 
  mutate(r = map(vars, \(x) cor_pool(imp_overall, x[1], x[2])),
         `SD ratio` = map(vars, \(x) sdratio_pool(imp_overall, x[1], x[2])),
         `MA slope` = map(vars, \(x) MA_pool(imp_overall, x[1], x[2])),
         var = recode_values(var,
                             "air_t_mean" ~ "Mean air temperature",
                             "precipitation" ~ "Precipitation")) |> 
  select(!vars) |> 
  pivot_longer(r:`MA slope`) |> 
  unnest_wider(value) |> 
  mutate(across(est:hi, \(x) round(x, 2)),
         out = str_c(est, " (", lo, "–", hi, ")")) |> 
  select(var, name, out) |> 
  pivot_wider(names_from = name, values_from = out)

itp_ofd

write_csv(itp_ofd, "output/itp_ofd_comparison.csv")
```

# Save results

```{r}
#convert mids to list of dataframes, clean columns, calculate annual means
finish_weat <- function(x, fd){
  x |> 
    #keep only data for FD survey years
    semi_join(dates |> 
                select(site, survey_year) |> 
                mutate(across(everything(), as_factor))) |> 
    #keep only weather variables
    select(!any_of(c("month", "year", "cover", "above", "below", "overall"))) |> 
    #calculate 12-month means for each survey
    group_by(site, survey_year) |> 
    summarise(across(everything(), mean), .groups = "drop") |> 
    #precipitation multiplied by 12 because it's an extensive property
    mutate(across(contains("precipitation"), \(x) x * 12)) |> 
    rename(year = survey_year) |> 
    #join FD outcome
    inner_join(results_sites |> 
                 select(all_of(c("year", "site", "subplot", fd))) |> 
                 mutate(across(c(site, year), as_factor)),
                        relationship = "one-to-many") |> 
    #rearrange columns and pivot back to long
    relocate(any_of(c("subplot", "above", "below", "overall")), .after = year) |> 
    pivot_longer(5:last_col(),
                 names_to = c(".value", "type"),
                 names_sep = "_(?=[^_]+$)") |>
    #OFD not needed here
    filter_out(type == "OFD") |> 
    # CAM has no observed ITP data, those should probably not be used in models
    filter_out(site == "04-CAM1") |> 
    #remove unnecessary columns
    select(!c(type, solar_radiation_mean)) 
}

data_ITP_above <- complete(imp_above, action = "all") |> 
  lapply(finish_weat, "above")

data_ITP_below <- complete(imp_below, action = "all") |> 
  lapply(finish_weat, "below")

data_ITP_overall <- complete(imp_overall, action = "all") |> 
  lapply(finish_weat, "overall")

#join FD outcome for OFD
data_OFD <- complete_OFD |> 
  map(\(x) x|> 
        mutate(across(c(site, survey_year), as_factor)) |>
        inner_join(results_sites |> 
                     mutate(across(c(site, year), as_factor)), 
                   by = c("survey_year" = "year", "site" = "site"),
                   relationship = "one-to-many") |> 
        mutate(survey_year = fct_drop(survey_year)) |> 
        rename(year = survey_year)
  )


#save
save(data_OFD, data_ITP_above, data_ITP_below, data_ITP_overall, file = "intermediate/weather.RData")
saveRDS(weat_imp_raw, "intermediate/weat.rds")
saveRDS(dates, "intermediate/dates.rds")
```
